description:
About Trener

Trener is a Physical AI company building software-defined robotics for industrial automation. Our platform is built on the ROS 2 ecosystem, and our product, Acteris, is running in production with real customers on real factory floors — not in a demo lab.

Backed by a $32M Series A, we operate from dual headquarters in San Jose, California and Trondheim, Norway, with teammates across six countries. We work by four values: Move Fast Together, Earn Customer Champions, Deliver with Excellence, and Challenge the Possible.

The role

You will turn VLA research into robot behavior that works on a production line. Industrial work cells are high-mix and unforgiving: parts vary, lighting changes, and a policy that succeeds 80% of the time in simulation is not a product.

As a Robotics Research Engineer in T-Labs, you will own the full loop — data, training, evaluation, and on-robot deployment — for foundation-model-based manipulation policies. You will work alongside our AI compute, perception, and integration engineers to move models from paper to pilot to customer deployment.

What you’ll do

 - Design, train, and fine-tune Vision-Language-Action models for industrial manipulation tasks such as pick-and-place, kitting, machine tending, and assembly.

 - Build and scale robot learning data pipelines: teleoperation and demonstration collection, data curation, augmentation, and synthetic data from simulation.

 - Adapt pretrained vision-language backbones to robot action spaces, including action tokenization, diffusion or flow-matching action heads, and multi-camera inputs.

 - Define evaluation protocols and benchmarks that measure real-world success rate, robustness, and generalization to new parts, cells, and instructions.

 - Close the sim-to-real gap using simulation environments (Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, or Gazebo) and domain randomization.

 - Deploy policies on physical robots through ROS 2, working with the AI Compute team to meet latency and memory targets on edge hardware (quantization, distillation, TensorRT).

 - Track and reproduce state-of-the-art research, and share findings through internal tech talks, write-ups, and — where appropriate — publications at venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, and IROS.

 - Partner with Product, Integration, and customer-facing teams to turn customer use cases into learnable tasks and measurable milestones.


What you’ll bring

 - MS or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical/Mechanical Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent industry experience.

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience in robot learning, imitation learning, or reinforcement learning applied to manipulation.

 - Direct experience training or fine-tuning large multimodal models (VLMs, VLAs, or transformer-based policies) in PyTorch or JAX.

 - Strong Python skills and working proficiency in C++.

 - Experience running learned policies on physical robot hardware, not only in simulation.

 - Familiarity with ROS or ROS 2.

 - Comfort with distributed GPU training and experiment tracking (e.g., Weights & Biases, MLflow).

 - A track record of shipping research into working systems, and clear communication across research and engineering teams.


Nice to have

 - Publications at CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS, ICML, or CVPR on robot learning or embodied AI.

 - Contributions to open-source robot learning projects.

 - Experience with diffusion policies, flow matching, or world models for control.

 - Hands-on work with industrial arms (e.g., UR, ABB, KUKA, FANUC) and grippers, force/torque sensing, or tactile sensing.

 - Experience optimizing models for edge inference (quantization, pruning, distillation, TensorRT, NVIDIA Jetson).

 - Background in large-scale teleoperation or data collection infrastructure.

 - Experience at a robotics startup or in a production manufacturing environment.
